summary: A local wellness series that began September 7, 2023 teaches sleep hygiene, with a strong emphasis on turning off phones before bed. Experts cover blue light and melatonin, nutrition, mindfulness, a tech detox challenge, and family sleep routines. The workshops are hands-on, include personal manifestos, and are set to run until the end of October as a grassroots movement.
one_line: A town's sleep hygiene workshop series, running from September 7, 2023 to end of October, promotes switching off phones for better, more restorative sleep.
key_facts: The sleep workshop series began September 7, 2023 and is set to run until the end of October.
The first workshop was titled "Dream Without Screens: Harnessing The Power of Sleep Hygiene" and featured sleep hygiene expert Dr. Evelyn Saunders.
Dr. Evelyn Saunders said: "A restful night's sleep is the cornerstone of your well-being."
Clinical psychologist David McMullen presented on September 15 that phones harm sleep; blue light from screens suppresses melatonin production.
In a hands-on activity, participants compared sleep quality with and without phone use before bed, and nearly everyone reported improved sleep without the phone.
Nutritionist Lisa Chang's September 22 seminar, "Eat to Dream: Nutritional Guidance for Better Sleep," taught sleep-inducing meals rich in magnesium and tryptophan.
Wellness coach Mike Rivera led "Mindfulness and Moonlight: Preparing Your Mind for Sleep," using meditation and mindfulness for nighttime rituals.
Julie Tanaka, a tech analyst and former insomniac, leads the "Nocturnal Tech Detox Challenge" begun September 29, urging people to progressively cut phone use in the hour before bed.
Pediatric sleep specialist Dr. James Peterson's lecture "The Family Sleep Revolution" stressed a unified approach to family bedtime routines.
Workshops include sleep tracking and analysis, stress-reduction exercises, and group discussions about barriers to turning off technology at night.
Participants are urged to draft a personal manifesto of sleep hygiene commitments under the message "You are what you sleep."
The article reports local effects such as a café owner's tech-free week and a high school teacher integrating sleep education into their curriculum.
